primary_decoupling.activity_to_decouple: A2: Research and compare insurance options (coverage, price, terms, provider trust)
primary_decoupling.from_incumbent_bundle: Traditional insurers and broker/distributor flows that bundle education/comparison with the sales/activation step, plus fragmented customer self-research across multiple provider sites and documents (E8).
primary_decoupling.customer_pain: Researching and comparing policies requires customers to interpret complex coverage/terms, reconcile options across providers, and build trust before purchase—work that is time-consuming and cognitively heavy in the insurance CVC (E8).
primary_decoupling.new_offering: Launch an embedded “Coverage Explainer + Comparator” SDK/API that partners can drop into their app checkout: users answer a few questions, then receive plain-language coverage summaries and side-by-side comparisons across available embedded options, with contextual recommendations powered by automation/AI. This is a focused decoupling wedge consistent with Teixeira’s notion of “peeling away a portion of the customer’s value chain” (books/unlocking-the-customer-value-chain-chapter-1.md) while improving a single weak-link activity (E10, E11).
primary_decoupling.why_customer_switches: From the customer POV: “I can understand what I’m buying and pick the right protection inside the app I’m already using—without hunting across multiple insurer pages or deciphering policy language—and I still complete purchase in the same partner flow” (E7, E8, E11).

do_not_decouple.activity: A6: File a claim and track resolution; then renew/continue or exit coverage
do_not_decouple.reason: Avoid making claims handling the decoupling wedge: it is operationally heavy and deeply tied to carrier processes; pushing into this too early increases delivery risk and can distract from Trov’s partner-integration pivot (E6, E7, E8).

do_not_decouple.activity: A3: Purchase/activate coverage at the moment of need (on-demand or embedded)
do_not_decouple.reason: Do not lead with unbundling/owning the full purchase/activation step end-to-end; Trov’s transition objective is to scale via embedded partner integrations, not to rebuild a standalone DTC checkout that competes with partner-native purchase flows (E6, E7, E9).

do_not_decouple.activity: A4: Onboard and set up the policy (confirm identity/item details, receive policy issuance and documentation)
do_not_decouple.reason: Avoid making onboarding/issuance the initial wedge because it is more integration-dependent with underlying insurer issuance workflows; it should be sequenced after discovery/comparison proves conversion lift within partner ecosystems (E7, E8, E11).

do_not_decouple.activity: A5: Manage coverage over time (turn on/off, adjust coverage, monitor protection, handle premium payments where applicable)
do_not_decouple.reason: Do not unbundle premium billing/payment ownership early; while Trov has strength in digital “Use & Management” from its original model, expanding immediately into payment rails and ongoing premium collection adds complexity that can dilute the focused decoupling wedge (E8, E12, E6).
